subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write/CAS fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects persisted exec approval security state and overlaps an open conflicting security PR plus closed direct fix attempts, so another automated branch should not choose the security-boundary design on its own.

options.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
options.body: Refresh a shared lock/CAS merge primitive on current main and use it for both allow-always persistence and usage metadata writes before closing this issue.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always repair
options.body: Limit the fix to concurrent allow-always entry persistence if maintainers want to defer the broader node metadata writeback security work.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open until the node stale-writeback security PR is either landed or replaced, then reassess whether a narrower race remains.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
recommendation.body: Refresh a shared lock/CAS merge primitive on current main and use it for both allow-always persistence and usage metadata writes before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest recent owner signal for exec approvals persistence and node/gateway approval policy history.
